subject: Audit log exportability & deletion evidence — Finvero ask
content:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finvero.com>

Cc: legal@finvero.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on audit/access log retention, exports and proof of deletion

Hi Markus —

Thanks for taking this. We have a few compliance checkpoints before we can sign off on the Data Processing Addendum. Short list below — can you confirm if Redwood can meet these and, if so, what the delivery model looks like?

1) Retention windows: for tenant-level audit logs and access traces, what are the configurable retention periods we can choose from (minimum, default, maximum)?
2) Export formats & filters: can we export raw logs for a tenant scoped to a time range, and in which formats (JSONL, CSV, parquet)? Any limits on file size/slicing?
3) Proof of deletion: after we request a delete for tenant data (audit logs included), what evidence does Redwood provide that logs were erased from production and backups? Time-to-delete SLA?
4) Legal hold: if we place a legal hold on a subset of records, does that pause deletion/export flows or is there a separate preservation workflow?

We need this in writing to present to our InfoSec and Legal teams. Appreciate a brief technical answer and an example timeline for a typical export request (e.g., 90 days of logs for a single tenant).

Best,
Elena

Hi Elena —

Thanks — high level answers inline below, then I attached a short export playbook and a retention matrix for options. Happy to schedule a quick screen to walk through specifics.

1) Retention windows:
- Minimum: 7 days configurable for transient debug traces.
- Default: 90 days for audit/access logs on hosted plans.
- Maximum: up to 7 years on Dedicated/Private with an archive tier, subject to contract.

2) Export formats & filters:
- Supported: JSONL (primary), gzipped CSV for tabular slices, and Parquet export for large bulk jobs via our archive pipeline.
- Filtering: tenant_id, time range, event types (AUTH, TOKEN, ADMIN_API, ROUTE), and request_id.
- Slicing: exports are chunked at ~10GB compressed to keep transfer stable; we provide a manifest describing slices.

3) Proof of deletion:
- We provide a deletion certificate: a signed manifest listing deleted object ids, time of deletion, and erasure job run id.
- Backups: standard backups are on a 30-day rotation; deletion jobs mark corresponding objects for removal in the backup lifecycle and we record the erasure passes.
- SLA: standard erase completion for audit log objects: 72 hours for hosted API tenant requests; 7 days for archive-tier and cross-region erasures (longer due to multi-stage workflows).

4) Legal hold:
- Legal hold triggers a preservation workflow: records under hold are marked immutable and excluded from normal deletion jobs. Exports can still be run for held records but they will be retained until hold is lifted.

Attached: export_playbook.pdf and retention_matrix.xlsx (see notes column for Dedicated/private differences).

Next steps: if you need an example export manifest, I can attach a redacted sample.

Best,

Hi Elena —

Adding a quick, concrete sample and the operational steps so you can share with Legal. I've attached two redacted samples: audit_export_manifest_sample.json and a compressed example slice name pattern. Key notes below:

- Manifest: includes slice_id, start_time, end_time, tenant_id, event_count, checksum (sha256), and storage_path. We include a signed metadata block (Ed25519) that our certificate rotation signs.
- Export cadence: ad-hoc exports are queued; for a 90-day export for a single tenant (approx. 120GB compressed), typical turnaround on hosted: 24–72 hours depending on queue/backfill. For Dedicated customers with burst Egress, same-day is possible.
- Deletion certificate: we emit a signed deletion manifest that contains deleted slice_ids, deletion_timestamp, erasure_job_id, and the sha256 digest of each slice prior to deletion. That digest is logged and included in the certificate for chain-of-custody.
- Backup lifecycle: for hosted tenants we mark slices for deletion and then a separate erasure sweep removes them from backups during the next backup rotation; we record a secondary confirmation once the sweep completes (this is the second confirmation you'd see within up to 30 days).

Attachments in this message: audit_export_manifest_sample.json (JSON, redacted), retention_matrix.xlsx (XLSX), export_playbook.pdf

Rishi — tagging you on legal-hold language in case Finvero needs contract-level preservation clauses.
